meta.title: About Betty Teklemariam, intercultural advisor and mediator
meta.description: Betty Teklemariam is an intercultural advisor and cultural mediator. Social pedagogue, born in Asmara, working with the Eritrean community in the Netherlands since 2000.

schema.description: Intercultural advisor and mediator between Eritrean communities and Dutch organisations. Social pedagogue, working in the Netherlands since 2000.

hero.title: About Betty Teklemariam
hero.intro: I've worked with Eritrean communities since 2000 and know both sides of the conversation: as a social pedagogue and from my own experience.

story.heading: My story
paragraphs: I was born in Asmara, Eritrea. At a young age I had to flee, and I ended up in a completely new environment. I experienced first-hand how important support and understanding are to feeling safe and heard. That became the foundation of my work.
In Germany I studied Social Pedagogy and then worked for years in youth care and psychiatry, supporting migrants with complex psychosocial issues. In 2000 I came to the Netherlands.

Since then I've worked with Eritrean and Ethiopian refugees and status holders, and with the professionals around them. Connection, trust and tailored support are the three things I steer by in every case.

timeline.heading: From Asmara to the Netherlands
timeline.intro: The route that shaped my work, from my own experience as a newcomer to intercultural advisor and mediator.

expertise.heading: What Betty brings
expertise.intro: Three kinds of knowledge that come together in every case.

items.title: Cultural knowledge
items.desc: Norms, communication patterns, gender roles and family context within the Eritrean and Ethiopian community.

items.title: Pedagogical & social knowledge
items.desc: Social pedagogue with a background in youth care and psychiatry. Experience with trauma, parenting issues and unsafe situations within families.

items.title: Practical experience
items.desc: Since 2000 I've guided families, women and children, and advised organisations, especially where standard approaches fall short.

languagesBlock.heading: Languages
languagesBlock.note: I work in Dutch, Tigrinya, German and English, and understand the cultural context behind each language.

mission.quote: My mission is to build bridges between people, cultures and organisations. I believe that lasting support starts with trust, mutual understanding and a culturally sensitive approach that does justice to the background and the possibilities of every individual and family.
